newsitem.title: USA: Orange County board approves airport plan.
newsitem.headline: Orange County board approves airport plan.

text.p: The Orange County California Board of Supervisors on Wednesday backed a controversial plan to build a commercial airport at the county's El Toro Marine Corps Air Station.

The board's decision, certifying the environmental impact report for the proposed commercial passenger and cargo airport, followed over 12 hours of public comment and deliberations Tuesday and Wednesday.
Further environmental studies will now be conducted, Kathleen Chambers, a county spokeswoman, said. She said this review process could take several years to complete.
The supervisors called for the development of an airport master plan that would include an analysis of service levels ranging from 10 million to 25 million passengers annually.
The supervisors said they would study the feasibility of having a two-airport system in Orange County, which would include continued commercial passenger operations at John Wayne Airport.
County supervisors had considered three re-use options -- a commercial passenger and cargo airport, a commercial cargo and general aviation airport, as well as non-aviation uses.
The El Toro base is scheduled to be converted to civilian use by 1999.

Earlier this year, a study of future uses of the El Toro Marine Corps Air Station concluded that converting the station into an international airport would pump nearly $10 billion a year into the area's economy.
The draft environmental impact report found that an international airport that could serve more than 38 million passengers a year would cost $1.6 billion to build.
